title: Chain inspection: Even-key census
topics: Linked lists, binary trees and search trees
summary: Traverse the supplied acyclic linked list from head to tail and produce its node values in that order. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.
descriptionMd:
Index cards are joined by individual links rather than stored in numbered drawer slots. Ivo separates readings for the office's even-numbered keys. A zero reading belongs in that count, just like any other even number.

Traverse the supplied acyclic linked list from head to tail and produce its node values in that order.

Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values.

Implement chainInspectionEvenKeyCensus(head, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Linked traversal. Traverse the supplied acyclic linked list from head to tail and produce its node values in that order. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
Lists are acyclic. Trees use level-order JSON with null for missing children; [] is an empty root. The runner supplies nodes with val/next or val/left/right.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with linked traversal. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
Traverse the supplied acyclic linked list from head to tail and produce its node values in that order. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,-3,7,0,12]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 2.
The derived sequence is [4,4,-2,4]. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 4.
The derived sequence is []. Return how many values in the derived sequence are even, including 0 and negative even values. This gives 0.

overview: Counting variation: Linked traversal. Build the sequence once, then report exactly what the inspection card requests.
